headline: Chinese AI models now trail their US rivals by only about 3% on benchmark scores, according to a new Bloomberg Intelligence report.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: a credible analyst's view of a narrowing gap, but based on benchmarks and one analyst's reading.
importance_line: The finding feeds the debate over US chip export limits and over how long American labs can charge premium prices, but it rests on one leaderboard and the analyst himself warns that rankings shift.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Robert Lea found the gap between top US and Chinese AI models has shrunk to about 3% on benchmark scores, from about 15% earlier this year, after DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash release in September. DeepSeek scored 81.1 on LiveBench, a public ranking, against 83.4 for Anthropic's best, yet only three of the top 15 models are Chinese, and Lea cautions that rankings shift and that Chinese firms may stay unprofitable until 2030.
notes: Bloomberg blocked; text read via The Edge Malaysia (carries Bloomberg's report). url is the Bloomberg original.
